added_failures_basis: The reviewed run was dispatched unarmed: its manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite. This review measured the reviewed node's declared ruff gate in two scratch trees extracted with git archive from the reviewed commit's own object store into $TMPDIR/arms-jtfig (no worktree created): base arm gate-base.log (revision 7e975e9c: ruff check imas_ambix tests, All checks passed!, EXIT=0) and head arm gate-head.log (revision c35e1783: ruff check imas_ambix tests scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py, All checks passed!, EXIT=0). The reviewed node's substantive check is the count guard the script prints and asserts, which reads the real JT-60SA description store and cannot run on this host's lane; it was read from the reviewed run's own script-run.log (both phases, all six counts equal to the store, EXIT=0). Non-pytest gates report no FAILED node ids, so both arms are empty: head failing ids minus base failing ids is 0.

findings.text: follow-on: the node's only assertion is _report's count-equality guard, and nothing in the test suite can reach it. _report compares the drawn counts against the store's counts and raises SystemExit on a mismatch (line 135), and the reviewed run demonstrated it fires (probes 17->16 refused, negative-control.log). But the guard runs only when the script is executed against the real JT-60SA description store under /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/machine_description, which is a heavy, data-coupled run this lane must not perform; no file under tests/ imports or exercises scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py (grep -rln figures_jt60sa tests/ returns nothing). A regression that broke the machine-map addressing, the IDS reads or the extract/render call would not fail the suite -- only a worker who re-runs the script on the data (or its negative control) would see it. Durability is scored 8 on that basis. The done-when named no test, so this is recorded as a follow-on, not a defect this commit introduced.

item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to render the JT-60SA OP1 and OP2 geometry figures through imas-ink. The commit adds scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py which loads load_packaged_machine_map('jt-60sa'), opens each phase through NetCDFTransformEngine.open, reads wall/pf_active/magnetics with imas.DBEntry, and renders both phases via imas_ink.extract.extract_geometry and imas_ink.figures.geometry_figure_mpl in DEFAULT_STYLE; both landed SVGs carry drawn geometry (68 <path> plus rects and 88 <use> markers each) and the reviewed run's script-run.log shows both phases rendering with every count equal to the store.
